title: ÆTHER: Zero Hour (modern action blockbuster main theme)
story: A cyber attack blacks out today's Mumbai at midnight; one young agent races the clock across rooftops and highways to switch the city back on.
script:
# Zero Hour: outline (written before the music)

**Genre:** modern big-screen action thriller, main title theme. About 90 s, hype from the first second.
**Story:** Mumbai, today. At midnight a cyber attack blacks out the whole city. One young undercover agent has 60 minutes to reach the control tower and switch the city back on, chased across rooftops, highways and the sea link.
**Feeling:** pressure, speed and swagger from the start, rising to a huge victory when the lights return.

| Time | Scene | Music |
|---|---|---|
| 0-3 s | The skyline goes dark in one wave, block by block. | One huge low boom and a brass blast, then the 3-note call on a gritty synth. |
| 3-14 s | Red emergency lights. The agent's eyes open in the dark. | Ticking clock pulse, deep synth bass, low male choir, strings pumping fast. |
| 14-26 s | She sprints across rooftops, a drone behind her. | Hybrid drums and a real thavil kick in; the main hook on synth lead and brass together. |
| 26-38 s | Bike chase down the dark highway, sparks and headlights. | Hook passes to a fiery solo violin with slides; driving strings; choir shouts on the accents. |
| 38-50 s | Freeway pile-up; she flips over the car and keeps running. | Bigger: brass and choir carry the hook, the drums double up. One beat of total silence, then a slam. |
| 50-64 s | Face-off with the hacker in the control tower. | A bansuri stabs the hook in fast runs, answered by the synth lead; tension rises. |
| 64-80 s | She pulls the switch. The city lights up again, wave by wave. | The hook a whole step higher, full orchestra, choir and drums, the biggest moment. |
| 80-90 s | She walks out into the bright city. Title: ZERO HOUR. | Three rising hits, a final boom, and the 3-note call on brass. |

**Raga:** Shanmukhapriya in E (dark, fierce, with a sharp edge). One hook all the way through, one continuous generation.

brief.notes: Jithesh 30 Oct 11:30 on Midnight City: 'initial and mid part both are really boring... we need that hype, it's a cinematic world... not for DJ or concert, it's for the cinematic world, so think big.' Modern concept kept (11:21). Hype from second 0 (rule 9.13), hook every ~12 s (9.11), orchestra + choir + hybrid drums with electronic lead and Carnatic instruments as 2nd/3rd layer. Shanmukhapriya in E so the E G B logo call sits in the raga. Prompt mode, music_v2, one continuous generation.

prompt: A huge modern blockbuster film score, the main title theme of a big-screen action thriller set in today's Mumbai: a cyber attack blacks out the city at midnight and one agent races the clock to switch it back on. Cinematic, epic and hyped from the first second to the last: full symphony orchestra with powerful brass and fast driving strings, a big male choir chanting wordless syllables, massive hybrid cinematic drums and deep synth bass, a gritty electronic synth lead. Written the way today's biggest South Indian film composers score a mass action sequence: a raga melody, swinging half-time mass bounce, stop-and-slam full-band hits, choir answering the hook, the hook coming back bigger each time. Not DJ music, not EDM, not a club or concert track: it is film music. Raga Shanmukhapriya in E: E F# G A# B C D. The hook hammers B C D E in tight unison stabs, then falls E D C B A# G F# E, with gamakam bends on G and C. ONE memorable 5-note hook, B C D E C, runs through the whole track, passed between instruments. One steady tempo, 104 BPM half-time feel, never stopping. Real instruments named as themselves are played by real musicians, close, natural and dry, no heavy echo: thavil, solo violin, bansuri flute. Quiet electronic layer: chopped glitching veena stutters, pitched-down mridangam hits, reversed veena swells into each section. 0-3 s: one enormous low boom with a full brass blast, then a gritty bent synth plays a 3-note call E G B with the last note bent up. 3-14 s: a ticking clock pulse, deep synth bass, low male choir hum, fast pumping strings, tension at once, already loud. 14-26 s: hybrid drums and a real thavil crash in on the mass bounce; the hook on synth lead and brass together. 26-38 s: the hook passes to a fiery solo violin with slides, driving strings, choir shouts HEY on the accents. 38-50 s: bigger: brass and choir carry the hook, the drums double up; one beat of total silence, then a full-band slam. 50-64 s: a bansuri plays the hook in fast runs, answered by the synth lead; rising tension, taiko-style tom rolls. 64-80 s: the hook returns a whole step higher in F#, full orchestra, choir and drums, the biggest and most triumphant moment. 80-90 s: a korvai ending, three rising full-band hits, a final boom, then the 3-note call on solo brass. Loud and big from the very start, no soft intro, no slow or quiet middle, no lull longer than one beat, no gaps, no fade-out, no side-chain pumping, no white-noise risers, no drop-and-build EDM structure, no lyrics.
